This is still vulnerable to evil maid. You need to be able to attest the system before you enter the PIN.

phoronixrly · Oct 24, 2026

tpm2totp used to do this, eliminating the need to divulge the secret used to unlock the TPM, I now see that it has not seen a commit in 2 years.

I also hear mjg59 is looking into encrypted swap hibernation support, so there's a slim chance there will be some development on the system-attestation front.

lakeviewterrace · Oct 24, 2026

Extraordinary how Linux continues to be 20 years behind Microsoft and Apple when it comes to FDE. This is a hilariously stupid level of complexity for something that should have a universal solution across distros by now.

This is literally a one click process in Windows (plus a couple shell commands to enable TPM+PIN).

I'm not disparaging the author in any way — he's merely documenting the stupidity.

Avamander · Oct 24, 2026

Fairly sure that if the correct GPOs are set, there is no need for any shell commands needed for a TPM PIN enrollment.

Windows and macOS both can do FDE with good UI/UX compared to Linux.

lakeviewterrace · Oct 24, 2026

This is 100% correct, my comment was referring to non-domain joined PCs with no policies set.

bubblethink · Oct 24, 2026

What problem is this solving though? The post says they're doing this to avoid typing passphrases. Why would you want the private key hidden in the tpm chip of that device? How will you decrypt if the laptop goes bust or if you move the drive elsewhere?

lakeviewterrace · Oct 24, 2026

> How will you decrypt if the laptop goes bust or if you move the drive elsewhere

Windows and Apple both generate a recovery key as part if the enrollment process which you can store offline.
